key_insight: Conditioning the decoder as well as the denoising network preserves structural detail and temporal consistency in conditional video generation. RefDecoder injects reference information into the decoder to reduce detail loss and mismatches with the input image.
problem_solved: Standard latent diffusion pipelines use heavily conditioned denoisers but leave decoders unconditional, causing loss of fine detail and inconsistency relative to the reference image when generating videos (especially in image-to-video and reference-guided tasks).
method: Introduce a reference-conditioned decoder (RefDecoder) that receives features from the input/reference image via cross-attention or modulation layers to guide reconstruction.
Integrate RefDecoder into the latent diffusion video pipeline so both denoising and decoding stages are explicitly conditioned on reference and temporal context.
Train with alignment and temporal-consistency objectives to preserve structure across frames while allowing plausible motion and detail synthesis.
impact: Provides higher-fidelity, more consistent conditional video generation that better preserves the appearance of the reference; useful for image-to-video, editing, and controllable content generation pipelines.
visual_elements: Architecture comparison: standard latent-diffusion (unconditional decoder) vs. pipeline with RefDecoder (decoder receives cross-attention from reference).
Side-by-side sample frames: input/reference image → output without RefDecoder → output with RefDecoder to show improved detail and consistency.
Attention/feature overlay showing how reference features influence decoder activations across frames (visualize cross-attention heatmaps).
Bar chart of qualitative/quantitative improvements (e.g., perceptual similarity, temporal consistency metrics) without naming specific numbers.
paper_title: RefDecoder: Enhancing Visual Generation with Conditional Video Decoding
paper_authors: Xiang Fan, Yuheng Wang, Bohan Fang, Zhongzheng Ren, Ranjay Krishna
